title: TF module release QA simulation and rollback scripts
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft that captures a pragmatic QA simulation framework and a set of lightweight rollback script patterns for Terraform modules used in Private (VPC / on-prem) deployments. The focus is on allowing module maintainers to:
- run a repeatable compatibility simulation against a synthetic cluster/state,
- validate the exact state changes a module release will produce, and
- provide a straight-path rollback that operators can run during an upgrade incident.

Context and constraints:
- Private deployments run across customer-managed VPCs and occasionally air-gapped on-prem clusters. We must avoid any release that requires manual db dumps or obscure state edits.
- Our modules are consumed by customer stacks pinned to exact module source/version strings; still, we must assume some customers will follow a range (e.g., ~> 1.4).
- Many breaking changes arise from: provider upgrades, resource renames, state layout changes (map->list), and moved responsibilities between modules (e.g., network module now owns subnets).

High-level strategy (safe-by-default):
1) Simulation first: always run a cloning simulation against a copy of a representative tfstate (see below).
2) Two-stage publish: publish a non-latest pre-release tag (e.g., 2.0.0-rc1) and run a rolling canary with internal test projects before marking stable.
3) Migration/compatibility helpers: provide migration scripts (terraform state mv / import) and unit test transforms in the module repo.
4) Rollback by pin: recommend pinning consumers to previous minor when breaking; provide scripted automated pin-and-apply steps.

Quick checklist (pre-publish):
- [ ] Update CHANGELOG with clear upgrade notes and explicit breakage lines.
- [ ] Add migration.sh and an annotated migration plan to the repo.
- [ ] Add simulation job in CI that runs against a cloned tfstate (see Simulation section).
- [ ] Add canary acceptance tests that assert zero-drift (idempotency) for typical consumer stacks.
- [ ] Prepare rollback helper script and docs in /docs/release-rollback.md

Simulation: how to run a dry-run against a representative state
1) Acquire representative state
   - Grab a snapshot of a production-like tfstate from an internal test customer or from our internal self-hosted testbed. Store it in an isolated test backend (GCS bucket or local file for air-gapped).
   - Redact any sensitive fields. Document the snapshot id in the run notes.

2) Create a simulation workspace
   - Create a new backend and workspace: 
     - backend: terraform backend config pointing to a copy of the tfstate (e.g., gs://redwood-sim-testbed/$RUN_ID.tfstate)
   - Example sequence (bash):
     RUN_ID="sim-$(date +%s)"
     cp gs://redwood-prod-states/customer-xyz.tfstate gs://redwood-sim-testbed/$RUN_ID.tfstate
     export TF_BACKEND_CONFIG="path=gs://redwood-sim-testbed/$RUN_ID.tfstate"
     terraform init -reconfigure -backend-config="$TF_BACKEND_CONFIG"

3) Reproduce module upgrade in place
   - In a temp checkout of the consumer stack, update module source to the new tag (e.g., github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/modules/network?ref=v2.0.0-rc1)
   - Run terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan. Capture plan output to artifact storage.
   - Inspect plan for: resource deletions, state moves, replacement operations, and provider changes.

4) Plan analysis heuristics (automation friendly)
   - Fail the simulation if: > 3 resources are destroyed without explicit migration script, or any resource with lifecycle.keepers is replaced, or provider major version changes without explicit compatibility notes.
   - Flag any detected rename (resource type or address change) and require a migration.sh snippet.

Migration helpers and patterns to include with module releases
- migration.sh (example):
  #!/usr/bin/env bash
  set -euo pipefail
  # Arguments: --state-backend <backend-conf> --mappings mappings.csv
  # mappings.csv contains old_address,new_address per-line
  while IFS=, read -r old new; do
    terraform state mv "$old" "$new"
  done < "$MAPPINGS_FILE"
- Provide terraform import examples for resources that cannot be moved programmatically.
- If provider upgrade is required, list exact provider constraints and pin recommendations.

Canary / QA plan (internal rollout)
- Create two internal projects: canary-1 and canary-2. Canary-1 receives the rc tag and is observed for 48 hours. Canary-2 receives a pinned minor upgrade path.
- Acceptance criteria: no drift after two apply cycles, no surprise deletions, smoke tests (app-level e2e) pass.
- Escalation: if canary fails, revert canary by pinning consumers back to previous module version and run terraform apply with --auto-approve on the canary workspace.

Rollback patterns (operational recipes)
1) Fast pin rollback (recommended primary method)
   - Rationale: most consumers pin in their stack file; updating the consumer stack to pin previous module is the least invasive.
   - Steps: 
     - Checkout consumer repo branch rollback/$RELEASE-ROLLBACK
     - Update module source ref to previous stable (e.g., ref=v1.9.3)
     - Run terraform plan and ensure plan is expected (ideally no destructive operations).
     - terraform apply -var-file=secrets.tfvars --auto-approve
   - Script template (rollback-pin.sh):
     #!/usr/bin/env bash
     set -euo pipefail
     OLD_REF="$1"
     sed -i "s/ref=\(.*\)/ref=$OLD_REF/" modules/network/module.tf
     terraform init -reconfigure
     terraform apply -auto-approve

2) State revert (fallback, use sparingly)
   - If upgrade included unavoidable state layout changes and consumers did not pin: restore the tfstate snapshot from backup.
   - Steps: 
     - Identify backup snapshot id (from state history service).
     - Lock state, replace remote state with snapshot, run terraform plan to validate.
   - Notes: this requires coordination with customer ops, downtime windows, and is high friction.

3) Partial resource re-creation with migration scripts
   - For cases where newer module introduced resource rename but migration scripts exist, run migration.sh against the target workspace, then terraform apply.

Incident runbook (short):
- Triage (15m): determine whether the problem is a module-internal change (breaking) or provider/environmental.
- Contain (30m): pin consumers to previous stable, or lock state and move canary off the release tag.
- Recover (1-4h): run rollback-pin.sh in affected workspaces; if state revert needed, escalate to SRE lead.
- Postmortem: capture root cause, update module changelog, and publish a customer-facing advisory where required.

CI integration suggestions (minimal):
- Add a job: simulate-upgrade (runs plan against cloned tfstate and stores plan artifact).
- Add a job: migration-tests (executes migration.sh against a staged workspace).
- Add a job: canary-deploy (applies module in an ephemeral internal project).
- Example GitHub Actions snippet name: redwood/tf-module/simulate-release@v1

Acceptance criteria for a release to be promoted from rc -> stable
- Simulation plan shows no >3 unexpected destroys across representative states.
- Migration scripts are present and tested in CI.
- Changelog contains explicit breaking-change instructions and suggested consumer patches.
- Two internal canaries run successfully for 48h with smoke tests green.

Notes / gotchas observed in past incidents
- Hidden provider defaults changed (e.g., a provider flipped default attribute) and caused resource replacement. Always test plan with provider constraint exactly matching the release notes.
- Moving responsibility across modules (e.g., network->platform) often results in address renames; plan automation must detect and require explicit mapping.
- Air-gapped customers: ensure migration documentation includes steps to run offline (export/import state files, step-by-step import commands).

Open action items (owners):
- Sanjay Patel: draft migration.sh templates for common rename patterns (due 2024-10-10).
- Leah Torres: add simulate-upgrade CI job to terraform-modules repo (due 2024-11-01).
- Owen Park: prepare rollback-pin.sh and test in internal canary (due 2024-10-18).
- Maya Chen: collate postmortem checklist and notification templates (due 2024-10-09).

Appendix: quick command cheatsheet
- Copy state to sim backend: gsutil cp gs://redwood-prod-states/customer-xyz.tfstate gs://redwood-sim-testbed/$RUN_ID.tfstate
- Init with backend: terraform init -reconfigure -backend-config=path=gs://redwood-sim-testbed/$RUN_ID.tfstate
- Plan to file: terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan
- Show changes: terraform show -json plan.tfplan | jq '.'
- State move example: terraform state mv module.old_module.azurerm_network.network module.new_module.azurerm_network.network
- Pin rollback sed example: sed -i 's/ref=v2.0.0-rc1/ref=v1.9.3/' modules/network/module.tf

If you have a sample tfstate we should test with, drop it in gs://redwood-sim-testbed and tag a run id in the ticket ENG-1987. This doc is intentionally pragmatic and script-forward; please push examples and failures to the linked PR so we can iterate.
